title: Application Gateway Ingress Controller and the Gateway API

videos.script: Lesson 11 put the shop on a cluster. This lesson is about the front door: how a request from outside reaches the right pod. {{ingress}} Kubernetes has had an answer for years, the Ingress. It can say a host, a path and a Service, and little else. Everything else became annotations, a different dialect for every controller. {{agic}} On AKS, one of those controllers is AGIC. It carries no traffic. It watches the cluster and rewrites an Application Gateway outside it, through Azure Resource Manager. The gateway sends requests straight to pod addresses, and it learns about a new pod only when that write arrives. {{gateway}} Then the Gateway API, which replaces the Ingress. It splits the front door into a class, a gateway and a route, one for each team that owns a part. You will send ten per cent of the shop's traffic to version 1.1, and watch the API server refuse three mistakes and accept a fourth. {{agc}} Last, Application Gateway for Containers, the Azure service that reads those resources, and its own pieces, a frontend and an association, in Bicep. {{kind}} No controller runs in this lab, so nothing here routes a request. Every object is real, and every status says who has not answered yet.
